doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: His father's band and hearing big bands on the radio
summary: His father worked full time in a small band with Lanny's uncle; Lanny heard the big bands on pop radio and kept playing violin.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: But you were aware that — he didn’t — did he play full time?
He played full time, wow. And plus he had the radio gig.

Yeah. And then they played a lot of — oh there were places like the Kit Kat Club and the Belvedere Club and there were sort of like jazz places. And later on, after the violin episode they would take me to hear the band rehearse and things. So actually it was a very fruitful time for music because the pop stations were playing all the heavy bands. I mean you know Benny Goodman, Tommy Dorsey, Basie, Duke, they were all on what would be the rock & roll channels now. So it was great. A great experience to hear that.
And his band, was it a big band or was it a combo?
No it was three saxes, just three saxes, a trombone and three trumpets and three rhythm. And my uncle played saxophone in that band too so I sort of had — they were all my heroes, all those people.
So the violin didn’t last too long?
